title: Core Implementation Ledger ORM Mapping
objective: Map ImplementationTask, ImplementationRun, and RunRelationship to the selected API SQLAlchemy Base and statically verify their PostgreSQL metadata without any database operation.
scope: Three API-Base SQLAlchemy core ORM records in the explicit quantmind2 schema.
Named keys, checks, indexes, restrictive foreign keys, version columns, and domain-derived enum checks.
Dialect-only PostgreSQL DDL compilation, targeted tests, ORM contract documentation, Project Memory updates, and one local commit.
explicit_non_goals: No detail ORM tables or formal Domain-to-ORM mapper.
No production Repository, Session, Unit of Work, transaction orchestration, database connection, credential access, migration, schema/table creation, create_all, or executed DDL.
No Manifest Parser/Indexer, Git consistency service, API, UI, TDX, Dataset Snapshot, Factor DSL, Optimization, Validation runtime, Registry, LightGBM, or Qlib change.
No Factor Lab, dependency, lockfile, runtime configuration, accepted ADR, or historical Implementation Run change.
No implementation of QM2-P0-002A2a2 or later tasks.

known_limitations: Only Task, Run, and RunRelationship are mapped; detail tables and Domain/ORM mappers are not implemented.
No migration, schema/table creation, live PostgreSQL, production Repository, Session, UoW, transaction, Parser/Indexer, API, or UI exists.
Version columns do not implement optimistic locking without a future Repository adapter.
Complete DAG cycle prevention and concurrent edge-admission race handling are not database-enforced.
Static DDL compilation used an existing SQLAlchemy 2.0.51 environment while production requirements pin 2.0.25.
Manifest schema v1 cannot encode exact next task QM2-P0-002A2a2, so its machine next-task field uses legal parent QM2-P0-002A2; context next-task fields use QM2-P0-002.
ruff was unavailable and was not installed.
The containing commit cannot be embedded self-referentially; Git history resolves it after commit.
unresolved_questions: Which relationship types may coexist for one source and target pair?
How will PostgreSQL prevent relationship-cycle races under concurrency?
How will pinned SQLAlchemy 2.0.25 and a real isolated PostgreSQL server be supplied for migration/integration verification?
rollback_information: Revert the single containing commit. No database, schema, migration, data, API, runtime, model, Qlib, UI, dependency, lockfile, configuration, accepted ADR, or Factor Lab rollback is required.
security_impact: ORM metadata contains no credentials and import performs no file, environment, network, Git, engine, session, connection, or DDL operation; domain secret-like checks remain authoritative.
data_lineage_impact: No research data changed; the mapping prepares a future derived Ledger query index while Git Reports and Manifests remain authoritative.
